**Verdict:** supports

## Interpretation
Build the product around this head. It predicts WHEN to cut, from audio plus the show's own recent rhythm, on professional operator data, with an effect several times anything the dance corpora yield. The dance-trained head shapes what happens between cuts and the beat grid phases the transients. Also worth carrying forward: on a corpus of this size a linear model on good causal features is a serious competitor, so every neural claim here needs the ridge next to it.

## Notes
HEAD B is deployable and the strongest component measured in this project. The head that gets both the audio and the operator's own recent rhythm predicts the next scene change at 1.805x the base rate against 1.250x for rhythm alone, a margin of +0.555 (CI [+0.385, +0.739]) on 86 held-out shows — nearly double the ridge probe's +0.315 and six times the plan's +0.09 gate.
Two cautions that belong next to that number. First, a 3.6 M-parameter Conformer given audio alone (1.347x) does WORSE than a linear ridge on the same 52 features (1.500x); with roughly 500 training shows the capacity is not free, and the gain comes from combining audio with rhythm rather than from depth. Second, an earlier version of this evaluation fitted the rhythm baseline on the test song itself, which inflated it from 1.25 to 2.79 and would have reported the model as far worse than the baseline; the baselines here are fitted on training songs only.

## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[a-causal-conformer-with-three-heads-b18294]].

## Measurements
- [[light-bas-minus-shift-null]]: before 0.1464 → after 0.0009  (Δ -0.1455, down ✗ predicted up)
- [[fid-light-kinetic]]: before 700.4 → after 114.0  (Δ -586.4, down ✓ predicted down)
- [[light-diversity-kinetic]]: before 6.306 → after 4.075  (Δ -2.231, down ✗ predicted up)

## Gates
- `G-causal`: PASS — future-perturbation leak 0.0 at cuts of 50/100/200/300 frames; attention is masked to the past and windowed, the depthwise convolution is left-padded
- `G-bas`: **FAIL** — model +0.0009, CI [-0.0024, 0.004] (includes zero) against real-mapped +0.1464 and beat trigger +0.0959. Mechanism found: the model's block A outputs are over-smoothed toward the corpus median, so its light flashes 6.5 times a second instead of the real 4.3 and does so uniformly. A dense uniform event train has a HIGH circular-shift null by construction, so even correctly beat-phased transients cannot show above it.
- `G-fid`: **FAIL** — FID(model, real) 114.0 against half the null 68.1; the beat trigger scores 700, so the model is 6x closer to dance-derived light than the baseline is, and still not close enough
- `G-div`: **FAIL** — model 4.07 against real 6.31, a ratio of 0.65 versus the 0.7 required. The collapse control behaves exactly as predicted: the MSE head's diversity across style samples is 0.000 against the flow head's 2.03, at equal block A accuracy (val-track R2 0.057 vs 0.035), so the generative head buys variety for free — there is simply not enough of it

**Verdict:** refutes

## Interpretation
**Failure mode:** `recipe_conditional`

Two fixes follow from the mechanism, and neither is 'train longer'. First, the block A / block C boundary was drawn from the literature and should be redrawn from the Stage 0b audit: on this corpus almost nothing clears the identity baseline, so almost everything belongs in the SAMPLED block, not the regressed one. Regressing an unpredictable channel does not produce a cautious estimate, it produces a flat line, and a flat line makes bad light. Second, the flow head samples each frame independently given the trunk state, so its variety is high-frequency jitter rather than the burst-and-rest structure real dance has; it needs to condition on its own previous output. Both are v2 work. Meanwhile the diagnostic to keep is the one that caught this: report the event RATE and the circular-shift null next to every Light-BAS, because a model can raise alignment and lose the comparison by flashing more.

## Notes
The machinery works and the corpus is the ceiling, as Stage 0b predicted.
What passed: causality is exact (leak 0.0), the model trains in 9 minutes on one RTX 5070, and the generative head does what the literature says it should — the MSE control collapses to 0.000 diversity while the flow head gives 2.03 at the same block A accuracy.
Block A on unseen tracks: mean R2 +0.035, best channels footfall rate 0.220, metrical level 0.082, vertical bounce amplitude 0.038. On unseen DANCERS +0.069. On unseen GENRES -0.183 — negative, meaning worse than predicting the mean, which is exactly what Stage 0b's finding predicts: what the model can learn from this corpus is genre-conditioned style, so removing the genre removes the skill.
Block B events: footfall AP 0.392 against a 0.347 base rate on unseen tracks, 0.655 against 0.572 on unseen dancers; hits show no lift at all. Consistent with Stage 0a — event phase belongs to the choreography.
The light-level gates fail for one identifiable reason rather than three. Predicting near the conditional median makes every channel smooth; a smooth descriptor stream drives a light that flashes constantly and evenly; and an even event train sits at its own circular-shift null however well each flash is phased. The metric is not being unfair — it is naming the failure the plan was built to catch.

## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[audio-predicts-lighting-events-when-the-scene-changes-even-though-it-does-not-pr]].

## Measurements

- [[event-ap-lift-audio-only]]: before 1.1938177347183228 → after 1.2974029779434204  (Δ +0.103585, up)

## Gates
- `beats-circular-shift-null`: PASS — observed marginal lift +0.0909x vs circular-shift null -0.1568 +- 0.0876 over 40 reps -> z +2.83, p 0.000. Required z>2.0 and p<0.05.

**Verdict:** supports

## Notes
POSITIVE -- the first non-null result in this project.

140 songs, 1376 events, 5-fold CV by song, horizon 1.0 s.

  rhythm-only baseline (no audio)   1.3241x lift over base rate
  audio only                        1.2974x
  rhythm + audio                    1.4151x
  audio's MARGINAL lift             +0.0909x

Circular-shift permutation null (40 reps; event count and rhythm preserved,
only audio alignment destroyed):
  marginal null    -0.1568 +- 0.0876  ->  observed z +2.83, p 0.000
  audio-only null  +1.1938 +- 0.0519  ->  z +2.00

GATE MET (preregistered z > 2.0, p < 0.05).

The null mean is NEGATIVE (-0.1568): under shift, adding audio features HURTS
the rhythm baseline via added variance. So the observed positive marginal is
not an artifact of extra parameters -- extra parameters cost you here, and
audio still wins.

WHY THIS WORKED WHERE LEVELS FAILED: on the level target persistence scored
+0.708 and audio's marginal was -0.005. That comparison was structurally
rigged. Moving to events removes the edge, and the SAME audio features that
were worthless become significant. The failure was the target formulation,
not the features and not the model.

CONFOUND, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED (probe_cut_vs_light.py, 36 songs, native 30fps,
968 events): the target derives from stage VIDEO, so a camera cut looks like a
lighting change, and concert video is edited on the music. If cuts dominated,
this would be audio->editing, not audio->lighting.
  median rise time 18 frames = 0.60 s   (a cut is ~1 frame)
  only 13.5% rise in <=2 frames
  only 8.4% revert to the pre-event state within 4.5 s
  57.6% move to a NEW state and stay there
Gradual and persistent = lighting-like, not cut-like. This does NOT prove the
absence of edit contamination -- that needs shot-boundary labels the dataset
does not ship -- but it bounds it as a minority of events.

SCOPE, stated plainly: z=+2.83 establishes the coupling EXISTS. It does not
establish it is large enough to build a rig on (+0.0909x lift is modest), and it
does not say WHICH audio property carries it. That attribution is the next
probe and it is project-defining: if plain ENERGY carries all of it, the
industry's L2 threshold triggers are already at the ceiling and 'semantic'
buys nothing.

On 'which looks like a lighting engineer did it' the dance-derived hybrid won 8 of 9 decided trials against the beat trigger on brightness-matched pairs; on 'which is on the music' it was 5-4, a tie, which is what the design predicts because both arms carry the same audio-phased transients.
What the rater's notes add, and this is the useful part: the discriminating cue was dynamics, not timing. T05 (beat trigger): 'too fast changes for light, but on the music actually'. So the hybrid loses when its envelopes are flat, and the beat trigger loses when it flashes on every beat. That is the same failure exp-009 measured in the model's light (85.8 events per clip against 30.1 real-mapped) seen through a human: a light that changes on every beat is 'on the music' and is not 'a lighting engineer'.

## Notes
Stage 0a built and measured. What it establishes:
(1) The pipeline is real: 1408 clips -> descriptors (30 channels, 3 blocks) -> canonical-rig DMX -> renders, 9 ms per clip; DMX encode/decode round-trips to quantisation error.
(2) FID_light on delta features discriminates (G2 passes by a factor of 20).

## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[the-audio-lighting-event-signal-is-carried-by-loudness-energy-if-true-the-indust]].

## Measurements

**Verdict:** supports

## Interpretation
2026-09-28 retrospective interpretation correction, not a new experiment: native supports does not establish the loudness-only ceiling asserted by this hypothesis. In the saved RPMC-L2 feature-family probe, energy lift 1.4704 versus its permutation null 1.4381 has p=.24, while spectral lift 1.7060 versus its null 1.4562 is positive evidence for non-energy information; the common rhythm baseline is 1.3241. Preserve the measurements and historical closure, but do not infer either a proven zero energy contribution or a unique MFCC-versus-spectral mechanism from these correlated-feature comparisons.

## Notes
REFUTED, and the refutation is GOOD NEWS for the project.

Energy is the ONLY family that fails to beat its own null. Marginal lift over
the rhythm baseline (1.3241x), 140 songs, horizon 1.0 s:

  family      dim     lift      marg        null            z       p
  energy        2   1.4704   +0.1463   1.4381+-0.0488   +0.66   0.240
  harmonic      2   1.3832   +0.0590   1.4609+-0.0550   -1.41   0.960
  openl3      512   1.4151   +0.0909   1.2794+-0.0539   +2.52   0.000
  spectral     10   1.7060   +0.3818   1.4562+-0.0593   +4.21   0.000
  timbre      128   1.6203   +0.2962   1.3302+-0.0582   +4.98   0.000

THREE FINDINGS:

1. ENERGY IS NOT SIGNIFICANT (z=+0.66, p=0.240). Loudness does NOT
   explain when a lighting operator changes the scene. This directly contradicts
   the assumption behind FFT-threshold rigs. The industry's L2 approach is not
   at the ceiling here -- it is keying on the wrong feature.

2. TIMBRE (MFCC, z=+4.98) AND SPECTRAL (z=+4.21) CARRY THE SIGNAL.
   Operators respond to a change in the CHARACTER of the sound -- distortion
   coming in, a section changing texture -- not to it getting louder. On
   Rock/Punk/Metal livehouse material that is musically sensible: these genres
   are loud throughout, so loudness is uninformative while timbre is not.
   This is the specific, defensible claim that an L3 semantic model has
   headroom, and it NAMES the features that model must encode.

3. openl3 (z=+2.52) is BEATEN by 10 hand-picked spectral descriptors
   (z=+4.21) despite having 512 dimensions. The learned general-purpose
   embedding is not the right representation for this task. A bespoke encoder
   over spectral/timbral descriptors is better motivated than fine-tuning
   openl3 -- and it is far cheaper.

CAVEAT: 'timbre' here is MFCC. RPMC-L2 ships no zero-crossing-rate despite an
earlier schema note claiming it, so no separate percussive family was testable.
MFCC and the spectral descriptors are correlated; this probe establishes that
NON-ENERGY spectral character carries the signal, not which of the two is
primary.
